editorial.headline: Tax Consulting With a Clear Bali PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers tax advice, return preparation and non-legal representation—and remains open to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
Tax Consulting Activities covers the practical work of helping business and individual clients navigate tax matters. Its stated scope includes preparing income-tax returns for businesses or individuals, providing tax-consulting services, and offering accounting-consulting services. It also includes advice and representation on a client’s behalf before tax officials or the tax court, provided that representation is not legal representation. The centre of gravity is therefore tax-facing professional support: preparation, advice, accounting consultation and non-legal client representation within the tax system.

The classification is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity is not confined in the record to one kind of enterprise size. A provider serving individual taxpayers through return preparation sits within the same recorded scope as one advising business clients, while the scope also accommodates work conducted before tax officials or the tax court on the client’s behalf. The boundary is explicit where representation is concerned: it is representation other than legal representation.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record presents this activity as open to foreign investment at the national level, without a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position should be read together with the Bali entry, rather than assumed to settle the provincial picture by itself.

For Bali, the recorded status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and the activity is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. For this activity, the record states that at the Besar scale its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is straightforward: a foreign investor can register this tax-consulting activity in Bali today under the recorded position. The national foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%; the Bali record adds no separate foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition.
